Subject: Slowdown during high-concurrency inference window

Hi Jonas,

We saw elevated tail latency and a number of timed-out requests between 02:45 and 03:30 UTC yesterday while running our nightly batch against the dedicated pool. Errors looked like transient 504s during token generation (mostly for long sequences). Our SREs captured a few example request IDs: r-5f7c1, r-5f7c8, r-5f812. Can you confirm whether this was on Redwood's side and whether you have an initial timeline? This impacted a couple downstream jobs and we'd like to understand risk for our compliance window next week.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Engineering, Starlend

--
Starlend, Inc.

Subject: Post-incident technical debrief & customer action checklist

Hi Elena and Starlend team — thank you for your patience. Attached is our consolidated RCA, a compact timeline CSV, and a recommended set of customer-side mitigations. Summary below.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Impact window: 2028-03-21T02:45:12Z to 2028-03-21T03:30:05Z
- Root cause: Concurrent autoscaler churn in your Dedicated GPU pool caused a temporary under-provisioning of warm KV-cache primed instances. A combination of (1) an autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration and (2) a scheduling race when scaling from 0->N resulted in a batch of requests hitting cold instances, which introduced a token-generation penalty and intermittent 504s.
- Scope: Affected approximately 0.7% of your daily inference traffic during the window (predominantly long-context requests > 2k tokens). No model corruption or data leakage was detected.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:45:12Z — traffic spike began; autoscaler observed increased queue depth and issued scale-up decisions.
- 02:47:03Z — first increased 5xx rate observed; our health checks on a subset of newly scheduled workers registered longer startup latencies due to KV-cache population.
- 02:50:28Z — transient 504s peaked; autoscaler completed node creation but routes were still favoring cooler instances.
- 03:25:12Z — cache priming completed across scaled nodes; error rate returned to baseline by 03:30:05Z.

Contributing factors:
- Autoscaler cooldown default of 120s was too short for the chosen instance image when cold-starting with KV-cache population.
- Scheduler routing policy preferred round-robin that did not bias toward cache-warmed nodes during scale events.
- Your workload had a higher-than-usual fraction of long-context generation batches in the same window (we can share aggregate metrics).

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Temporarily increased the autoscaler target warm capacity for your pool and forced a proactive warm-up prior to the next scheduled nightly run.
- Deployed a scheduler tweak that favors recently warmed nodes for batch routing for short time windows after scale events.
- Added telemetry slices to surface cold-starts by model and sequence length in the Console.

Recommended customer actions (checklist):
1) If possible, schedule long-context batch jobs to avoid simultaneous heavy windows across clients — we can add guardrails per workspace.
2) For critical nightly jobs, enable the "reserved warm capacity" toggle in Redwood Console for your dedicated pool (we already enabled this as a temporary safety net).
3) Consider adding a lightweight retry with jitter client-side for token-generation requests that are idempotent; our SDK supports a 2-attempt default.
4) Share a representative prompt set with us for a permanent quantization/warmup plan (we'll propose a cache-priming policy tailored to your sequences).

Attachments included: redwood-rca-20280322.pdf (full RCA), incident-timeline-20280322.csv (per-request timeline), mitigation-action-items.md (tasks and owners).

If you'd like a live walkthrough of the RCA and a runbook update session, we can set up a 30-minute slot tomorrow with karthik and our infra lead. Proposed times: 2028-03-24 10:00-10:30 PT or 2028-03-24 16:00-16:30 PT.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as a priority and will follow up with a long-term scheduler/autoscaler improvement plan and a date for when it gets deployed.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Elena — quick answers and next steps before our walkthrough at 10:00 PT: 

1) Autoscaler cooldowns: The change we applied immediately was a temporary increase to your pool's warm-capacity target and a lengthened cooldown for aggressive downscales. We plan a permanent autoscaler config update that respects image-specific warmup durations as part of our dedicated-pool improvements. We'll share the RFC and timeline in the next follow-up (target: deploy by 2028-04-10).

2) Scheduler tweak scope: The routing change is constrained to your dedicated pool only — it will not affect shared-hosted instances. We've implemented a pool-scoped flag that favors warmed nodes for a short stabilization window after scale events; default behavior for other pools is unchanged.

3) SDK retry snippet: added to mitigation-action-items.md (attached). For convenience, paste below:

// recommended lightweight retry (pseudo)
for attempt in 1..2:
  resp = client.generate(request)
  if resp.status != 504:
    return resp
  sleep(random_jitter_between(100, 400))
return error

4) Walkthrough confirmed: 2028-03-24 10:00 PT with karthik and myself. Calendar invite sent.

We'll also follow up with a week-of-status note once the scheduler RFC is ready. If you'd like us to run an automated warmup job before your nightly window on a permanent basis, we can add that to the mitigation plan as an opt-in.

Thanks again for partnering on this — we'll prioritize minimizing the chance of recurrence.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
